subject: tool:gdl-memory-graph
value: WHEN A GATE ASKS 'DID YOU RUN THE ARBITER', ITS EVIDENCE PREDICATE MUST MATCH THE ARBITER'S OUTPUT VOCABULARY AND NOT ONLY ITS NAME — AND THE FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS THIS PRODUCES IS INVISIBLE IN THE FIRING COUNT, VISIBLE ONLY BY READING THE WOULD-BE-REFUSED SET. Measured run 44 while calibrating the slot-arbiter advisory (GATE L, memory_graph/core.py): the trigger fires on 92 anchored corpus records, and an evidence predicate looking for the literal token `slotdiff` scored 43 of them as violations. Eight of those 43 quote the tool's own map VERBATIM and had plainly run it — `the slot map reads TARGET-ONLY slots 24 (2 uses) and 28 (3 uses) against OURS-ONLY 40 and 44`, `frame: target 56 ours 56 -- SLOT MAP IDENTICAL`, `target-only slots -56/16/56/60, ours-only -64/24/64/68`. Records cite an arbiter by pasting what it printed at least as often as by naming the binary, so a name-only predicate taxes exactly the lanes that did the work most thoroughly. Widening the predicate to `slotdiff | SLOT MAP IDENTICAL | frame: target N ours N | target-only slots | ours-only slots | (N uses)` took the miss set 43 -> 40 overall and 19 -> 16 among records written since 2026-09-01. TWO COROLLARIES, both measured on the same gate. (a) THE EVIDENCE PHRASES MUST BE STRICTLY MORE SPECIFIC THAN THE TRIGGER PHRASES, or a phrase satisfies the gate it fires: `slot map` is a trigger term and `SLOT MAP IDENTICAL` is an evidence term, and only the qualifier keeps them apart. (b) THE NEGATIVE SIDE, NOT THE POSITIVE SIDE, DECIDES WHETHER A SCREEN CAN BLOCK: this one shipped ADVISORY because 43% of the corpus (28% of recent records) would have been refused, and two earlier trigger drafts died on the negative side alone — a bare `frame N` mention took the population from 92 to 208 and the miss rate to 72% (reporting a frame size is the baseline template AGENTS.md asks for, not a decomposition claim), and `save set`/`save-set`, which belong to savedregs.py rather than slotdiff, were 20 of the first draft's 67 hits.
